'''Patrick Dehornoy'''  (11 September 1952 – 4 September 2019) was a mathematician at the [[University of Caen Normandy]] who worked on [[set theory]] and [[group theory]].

== Early life and education ==
Dehornoy was born on 11 September 1952 in [[Rouen]], France.<ref name="CV"/> He graduated from the [[Lycée Pierre-Corneille]] in 1971.<ref name="CV"/> He studied at the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École normale supérieure]] from 1971 to 1975 and completed his [[Ph.D.]] in 1978 at the [[University of Paris]], with a thesis written under the direction of Kenneth Walter McAloon.<ref name="CV"/><ref>{{MathGenealogy|22593}}</ref>

==Career==
Dehornoy was a researcher at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS) from 1975 to 1982.<ref name="CV"/> He was at the [[University of Caen Normandy]] as a Professor from 1983 to 2017 and as an Emeritus Professor from 2017 until his death.<ref name="CV">{{cite web |url=https://www.lmno.cnrs.fr/archives/dehornoy/perso.html |title=CV, tâches d'animation de la recherche |lang=fr |website=[[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]] |accessdate=31 December 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201231234950/https://www.lmno.cnrs.fr/archives/dehornoy/perso.html |archive-date=31 December 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref> From 2009 to 2013, he was an adjunct scientific director of the ''{{ill|Institut national des sciences mathématiques et de leurs interactions|fr}}'' (INSMI) at the CNRS.<ref name="CV"/> Dehornoy died on 4 September 2019 in [[Villejuif]], France at the age of 66.<ref name="SMF-obit">{{Cite web|url=https://smf.emath.fr/actualites-smf/deces-de-patrick-dehornoy|title=Décès de Patrick Dehornoy &#124; Société Mathématique de France|website=smf.emath.fr|accessdate=31 December 2020}}</ref>

==Research==
Dehornoy found one of the first applications of [[large cardinal]]s to algebra by constructing a certain left-invariant [[total order]], called the [[Dehornoy order]], on the [[braid group]].<ref>{{Citation | last1=Dehornoy | first1=Patrick | title=Braid groups and left distributive operations | doi=10.2307/2154598 | mr=1214782 | year=1994 | journal=[[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]] | issn=0002-9947 | volume=345 | issue=1 | pages=115–150| jstor=2154598 | doi-access=free }}</ref> In his later career, he was a major contributor to the theory of braid groups, including creating a fast algorithm for comparing braids,<ref name="Dehornoy 1997">{{cite journal |title=A Fast Method for Comparing Braids |journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]] |date=1997-02-10 |last=Dehornoy |first=Patrick |volume=125 |issue=2 |pages=200–235 |doi=10.1006/aima.1997.1605 | doi-access=free}}</ref> and was one of the main contributors to the development of [[Garside element|Garside methods]].<ref name="SMF-obit"/>

==Awards==
In 1999, Dehornoy received the [[Ferran Sunyer i Balaguer Prize]].<ref name="CV"/> In 2002, he was elected a senior member of the [[Institut Universitaire de France]] (renewed in 2007).<ref name="CV"/> In 2005, he received the {{ill|Prix Langevin|fr}} of the French Academy of Sciences.<ref name="CV"/> In 2014, he received the [[European Mathematical Society|EMS]] Monograph Award for his book ''Foundations of Garside Theory''.<ref name="CV"/>
